questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should stay right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders at the back watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What should you do if it starts to rain while you are riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil buildup and is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies even braking to both the front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers your braking habits.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking automatically when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space for better visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Use all four fingers to squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly. Gradually apply more pressure as needed.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to brake while riding in a curve?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gently.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: They do not need to reach the footrests.
They should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit right behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could block your controls.

questions.question: What is NOT a benefit of choosing the right lane position?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Block access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids blind spots, avoids hazards, stops others from sharing your lane, and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important when choosing a helmet?

options.text: The helmet does not have any defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly all around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for protection.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Do not worry about where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Being too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is the safest way to approach them?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Turning to hit the tracks at a right angle can be dangerous because it may send you into another lane.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down quickly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's larger brake lights. Flash your brake light to alert others, especially when you stop faster than expected.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often a person usually drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person usually drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip opposite to where you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn to lean the right way.

questions.question: When braking while turning:

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the turn.
You may have less traction as you lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the turn.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be careful. Some tire traction is being used to make the turn while leaning, so less traction is left for braking.

questions.question: When a group of riders exits a highway, which formation should they use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for normal group riding. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly, then slowly increase front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week before you ride. Regular checks are important for safe riding.

questions.question: Helmeted riders are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, no matter your speed.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals a hazard on the right side of the road. Hand signals help riders communicate with each other.
